aboutH2: Alcove Addiction Recovery for Women: Residential Treatment for Women in Calgary
intro: Alcove, known as Youville until 2015, is a residential treatment for alcohol or drug addicts. It is a long term drug and alcohol rehab which could even extend up to three years if that is necessary. It is for women only and moves through four houses: Elderberry House for 12 weeks of individual residential treatment, Willow House for the family program, Aspen House as a transitional recovery community and Juniper House for sober living. There is also a part of the program which can include the mothers and their children in a more independent living environment. The program is composed mainly of counselling, whether it is individual or in group. There is also a four-week online program for women who are waiting for a bed, preparing for treatment or back at home.

pillars.title: Named Houses on a Quiet Street in Altadore
pillars.body: Alcove's address is 1937 42 Avenue SW, a residential street in Altadore in southwest Calgary, about a kilometre south of the shops on 33 and 34 Avenue in Marda Loop. The centre calls its facilities home-like, and each stage of care has its own house name. Elderberry House holds the 12-week individual program and Willow House holds the family program, where mothers live with their young children. Recovery words and the Serenity Prayer are painted on the walls of the shared rooms. Residents can smoke or use non-refillable vapes in designated areas only.

pillars.title: A Women's Centre With Almost 50 Years in Calgary
pillars.body: The Grey Nuns opened Alcove in 1977 as a safe place for women dealing with addiction, trauma and life on the margins, and it took its current name in 2015. It is now run as a non-profit society. Marium Tahir, who trained in medicine with a focus on psychiatry, directs clinical services, and Priya Reynaud is chief executive. Several staff named on the website, both case workers among them, write about their own lived experience of addiction and recovery. Close to half of the women at Alcove identify as Indigenous, and Wellbriety, Elder visits, healing circles and ceremony teachings are offered to anyone who wants them.

pillars.title: Aspen House, Juniper House and a Sunday Meeting
pillars.body: Women who finish the 12 weeks can move into Aspen House, a short-term recovery community with shared chores, routines and life skills work before living on their own. In 2025, 22% of residents made that move. Juniper House comes next for women who are working or in school: sober housing with either a private bedroom in a shared two-bedroom suite or a whole suite, applied for by email at soberliving@alcoverecovery.ca. Alumnae and moms in recovery also meet every Sunday from 6:30 to 7:30 pm at Altadore Church, 4304 16 Street SW.

overviewH2: Alcove Addiction Recovery for Women: Centre Overview
overview: Every program at Alcove uses a trauma-informed, client-centred model built on Stephanie Covington's work with women. Days in residence mix individual and group counselling with skill-building workshops, mindfulness and meditation, breathwork and art-based processing, and peer support runs through the week. Evening recovery meetings are part of the routine.

Alcove does not stick to one recovery model. Its program page says residents are introduced to 12 Step, SMART Recovery and Dharma Recovery, and to the Wellbriety program for Indigenous cultural healing. Twelve-step ideas show up in daily life too: the Serenity Prayer is painted on a lounge wall, and graduates' stories mention working the steps. The website does not say whether attending outside AA meetings is required, so ask intake if that matters to you.
serviceCaption: 12 services · as described on the centre's website
afterOverview: Alcove publishes its own outcome figures. In 2025, 83 women came through its programs, 61.4% completed treatment and 75 children were part of the families it worked with. Across 2023 to 2025 the totals were 252 women, a 63% completion rate and 282 children. The centre says it is a licensed residential addiction treatment provider in Alberta, and its 2025 audited financial statements show about 70% of its revenue came from Alberta Health Services.

location.heading: Alcove Addiction Recovery for Women in Calgary, Alberta
location.intro: Alcove sits in Altadore in southwest Calgary, a few blocks south of Marda Loop and a short drive from the Elbow River and River Park. Downtown Calgary is about 15 minutes away by car, Okotoks about 35 minutes, Airdrie and Cochrane around 40 minutes, Red Deer about an hour and 45 minutes, Lethbridge about 2 hours 15 minutes and Edmonton roughly 3 hours 15 minutes.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.a: Alcove is for women aged 18 and older who want help with alcohol or drug use. Applicants must be clean and sober, and must not have gambled, for at least five days before admission, and must be physically and emotionally able to take part. The family program is for women who are pregnant or parenting young children.

faqs.q: Can I bring my children to Alcove?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are pregnant or parenting young children you can apply to the Residential Family Program at Willow House. It runs for 12 weeks and adds parenting classes and mother-child activities to the usual counselling. Mothers bring clothing and supplies for their children, such as diapers, bottles and a car seat or stroller.

Alcove does not publish a fee for its residential program. Applicants need confirmed funding before they are admitted, and the intake coordinator at 587-576-3512 can explain the options. The 4-week online program costs $100, and $25 comes back when you finish it.

The residential program lasts 12 weeks, in either the individual or the family stream. Women who complete it can move into Aspen House, a short-term transitional community, and later into Juniper House sober living, so the full path can last well beyond the first three months.

Partly. Alcove's program page says residents are introduced to several pathways: 12 Step, SMART Recovery and Dharma Recovery, as well as Wellbriety for Indigenous cultural healing. Evening recovery meetings are part of the residential routine. The website does not say whether outside AA meetings are mandatory, so ask intake before you arrive.

No detox is listed on Alcove's website. Women must be clean and sober for at least five days before admission and must not have taken restricted medications in that time, so anyone who needs medical withdrawal management should arrange it first.

faqs.q: How do I get admitted to Alcove?
faqs.a: Call the intake line at 587-576-3512 for a phone assessment. If you go on the waitlist, you need to check in every day by phone or email, and names are removed after two weeks without a check-in. Intake itself happens Monday to Thursday between 10 am and 2 pm, and admission has to be confirmed at least 48 hours ahead.

faqs.q: Where is Alcove and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Alcove is at 1937 42 Avenue SW in Calgary's Altadore neighbourhood, south of Marda Loop. It is about 15 minutes by car from downtown Calgary, around 40 minutes from Airdrie or Cochrane and about 3 hours 15 minutes from Edmonton.

Graduates can move to Aspen House for structured transitional living, then to Juniper House if they are working or in school and want sober housing. Alcove also hosts a weekly alumnae and moms recovery meeting every Sunday, 6:30 to 7:30 pm, at Altadore Church, 4304 16 Street SW.
